name: OpenClaw
summary: A self-hosted AI assistant centered on one long-lived Gateway that owns sessions, routing, events, and channel connections, with WebSocket clients, channel plugins, agent tools, and device nodes around that control plane.
scope: agent sessions, tools, and model providers
control UI, CLI, and device nodes

features.name: Single Gateway control plane
features.description: The fixed README and architecture documentation describe one Gateway process as the control plane and source of truth for sessions, routing, and channel connections. Clients including the Control UI, CLI, TUI, and nodes connect to it.
benefits: Centralizes routing, sessions, events, and channel ownership
Allows the same deployment shape to serve personal or shared use through configuration
costs: The Gateway becomes a concentration point for availability, authorization, and operational state
A single control plane does not imply single-process execution for every agent or tool action

features.name: WebSocket client and node protocol
features.description: The fixed architecture documentation specifies JSON text frames over WebSocket, a connect handshake, request/response methods, event subscriptions, and node clients with role, capabilities, commands, and device identity.
benefits: Provides one protocol boundary for operators, UIs, and device nodes
Supports request acknowledgements and streamed agent events
costs: Connection, pairing, identity, and reconnection states add protocol complexity
Device capabilities and permissions must be checked at invocation boundaries

features.name: Plugin channel routing surface
features.description: The fixed README describes messaging channels and plugins, and the fixed source exposes a registry facade for channel IDs, metadata, aliases, and plugin lookup. The claim is limited to the registration boundary, not the behavior of each channel implementation.
benefits: Adds channels without changing the central Gateway contract
Provides normalized identifiers and metadata for setup and routing
costs: Provider-specific delivery semantics and availability vary by plugin
Plugin registration and credentials expand the trust and lifecycle surface

features.name: Session-scoped agent and tool execution
features.description: The fixed README and architecture docs place agents, tools, skills, model providers, and sessions behind the Gateway, while the security documentation warns that tools run on the host for the main session unless sandboxing is configured.
benefits: Connects conversational sessions to model and tool capabilities
Makes sandboxing and inbound-message trust explicit operational boundaries
costs: Host-side tools can have broad effects if sandboxing and access policy are absent
Long-lived sessions and multi-agent routing require explicit identity and isolation policy

mathematical_views.question: How do connect, request, streamed event, final response, and shutdown transitions coordinate one Gateway client session?
assumptions: WebSocket text frames carry JSON protocol messages
A client connects and receives a hello/snapshot response before ordinary requests
Agent requests may be acknowledged, streamed as events, and finalized
The model abstracts internal persistence and provider execution

mathematical_views.question: How do channel plugins, senders, sessions, and agents map inbound messages to one Gateway-owned execution context?
assumptions: Channel plugins provide normalized identities and delivery adapters
The Gateway owns routing and session state
A route may select an agent/session according to configuration
The view does not infer that all channels have identical delivery guarantees

mathematical_views.model: Trusted control plane with untrusted ingress and effectful tools
mathematical_views.question: Which boundaries preserve operator control when inbound chat content selects agent and host-side tool behavior?
assumptions: Inbound messages are treated as untrusted input according to the README
Tool execution occurs on the host unless sandboxing is configured
Pairing, authentication, permissions, and sandboxing are deployment/configuration controls
This is a candidate security model, not a proof of safe deployment

benefits: One operational boundary for sessions and channels
costs: Gateway availability and policy become central dependencies

benefits: Unified interactive protocol for clients and devices
costs: Pairing, capability, identity, and stream lifecycle increase complexity

benefits: Conversational context connects to agent tools
costs: Host-side effects require sandbox and authorization discipline
